FSR-aware modification: The statement communicates an intermeeting, credibility-consistent 50 bp easing plus liquidity backstops (T-bill purchases, repos, administered-rate adjustments) to stabilize funding conditions and support demand as COVID-19 risks emerge. The Financial Stability Report had highlighted preexisting vulnerabilities—elevated asset valuations, high nonfinancial business leverage, and fragilities in short‑term funding markets (as seen in prior repo market strains)—that could amplify a negative shock. Those FSR-flagged vulnerabilities tilt the assessment more negative than the text alone implies. Offsetting this, the FSR also noted that banks entered the period with strong capital and liquidity and that household vulnerabilities were moderate, which supports transmission and limits downside tails.

Concise tone: Strong fundamentals but rising COVID-19 risks; decisive easing and liquidity support against an FSR backdrop of elevated corporate leverage and funding‑market fragility—net slightly negative, policy‑mitigated.
